translationRepairs: Liu Zao, whose courtesy name was Yansian, came from Yiyang in Guangping Commandery.
Liu Zao, whose courtesy name was Yanxian, came from Yiyang in Guangping Commandery.
During the Yong'an era he returned to Wei together with his brother-in-law Li Ni and was ennobled as Marquis of Yiyang.
During the Yong'an era he returned to Wei together with his brother-in-law Li Ni and was ennobled as Viscount of Yiyang.
易陽子 is a viscountcy (子), not a marquisate.
He was transferred to the post of General of the Dragon Chariot and commandant of the Yongcheng garrison.
He was transferred to the post of General of the Soaring Dragon and commandant of the Yongcheng garrison.
龍驤將軍 is General of the Soaring Dragon.

On a later southern campaign the emperor made Zao General Who Subdues the Barbarians and placed him in command of four armies under army supervisors such as Gao Cong as deputy commander of the eastern route.

On a later southern campaign the emperor made Zao General Who Subdues the Barbarians and placed him in command of four armies led by army commanders such as Gao Cong as deputy commander of the eastern route.
督統軍高聰等四軍: he commanded the army commanders, not under them.
At the opening of the Jingming era Emperor Xuanwu recognized his past service and appointed him secretary to the Grand Marshal.
At the opening of the Jingming era Emperor Xuanwu recognized his past service and appointed him adjutant (sima) to the Grand Commandant.
太尉司馬 is adjutant to the Grand Commandant.
He cultivated Liu Teng, who secured his appointment as director of the princely household.
He cultivated Liu Teng, who secured his appointment as director of the household of his fief.
國郎中令 serves Liu Teng's own fief.
He rose to chief assistant of his home province and then to an aide in the Ministry of Works, but was dismissed after an official scandal.
He rose to chief assistant of his home province and then to a subordinate on the staff of the Minister of Works, but was dismissed after an official scandal.
司空屬 is staff of the Minister of Works.

He had served as a staff officer in the garrison bureau under Cui Daogu at the Dongyang prohibition post. When Daogu surrendered, Yong went with him and was registered among the pacified commoners of Qi.
From the Dongyang guard post he became city bureau adjutant under Cui Daogu. When Daogu surrendered, Yong went with him and was registered among the pacified commoners of Qi.
自東陽禁防為崔道固城局參軍 describes a move from the guard post to the adjutant post.
When Wang Su governed Yuzhou, Yong served him as General Who Establishes Might and chief administrator for the southern command.
When Wang Su governed Yuzhou, Yong served him as General Who Establishes Might and chief administrator to the General Who Pacifies the South.
平南長史 is chief administrator of the Pacifies-the-South general's headquarters.
Su treated Yong, a veteran of the Wei court, with exceptional respect.
Su treated Yong, a seasoned scholar-official, with exceptional respect.
宿士 means a seasoned scholar, not a Wei court veteran.

Once his ambush was in place, Yong secretly sent men with gourds of fire across to the south bank and set them where the water ran deep, with orders that if fires appeared anywhere, they were to light theirs as well."

Once his ambush was in place, Yong secretly sent men with gourds of fire across to the south bank and set them where the water ran deep, with orders that if fires appeared anywhere, they were to light theirs as well.
Gongzheng was a cousin of Chao Zong, inspector of Qi Province.
Gongzheng was an elder paternal cousin of Zhao Chaozong, inspector of Qi Province.
從兄 is an elder paternal cousin; 超宗 is Zhao Chaozong.

Within two months he won two victories. Emperor Xiaowen was delighted and sent an envoy to Yuzhou to invest him as General of Distant Pacification for Yong'an, chief administrator of the southern headquarters, Administrator of Runan, and founding baron of Beiqiu with a fief of two hundred households.

Within two months he won two victories. Emperor Xiaowen was delighted and sent an envoy to Yuzhou to invest Yong as General Who Pacifies the Distant, chief administrator of the southern headquarters, Administrator of Runan, and founding baron of Beiqiu with a fief of two hundred households.
策拜永安遠將軍 = appointed Yong (永) as 安遠將軍; Yong'an is a misparse.
Pei Shuye besieged Woyang again. Emperor Xiaowen was then in Yuzhou and sent Yong as army commander with Gao Cong, Liu Zao, Cheng Daoyi, Ren Moqun, and others to relieve the city.
Pei Shuye besieged Woyang again. Emperor Xiaowen was then in Yuzhou and sent Yong as army commander with Gao Cong, Liu Zao, Cheng Daoyi, Ren Mowen, and others to relieve the city.
任莫問 romanizes as Ren Mowen.
Cong and his colleagues threw away their armor and fled straight to Xuanchi.
Cong and his colleagues threw away their armor and fled straight to Xuanhu.
When Yong reached Xuanchi, Emperor Xiaowen had the whole party put in chains.
When Yong reached Xuanhu, Emperor Xiaowen had the whole party put in chains.
During Prince Ying of Zhongshan's campaign against Yiyang, Yong served as General Who Pacifies the North and army commander, blocking the southern gate at the head of the long encirclement.
During Prince Ying of Zhongshan's campaign against Yiyang, Yong served as General Who Calms the North and army commander, blocking the southern gate at the head of the long encirclement.
寧朔將軍 is General Who Calms the North.
Xiao Yan's general Ma Xianbi pushed his camps forward step by step, hoping to lift the siege.
Xiao Yan's general Ma Xianpin pushed his camps forward step by step, hoping to lift the siege.
馬仙琕: 琕 is read pín.
At dawn Ma Xianbi came as Yong had foreseen. Zhang Huai's line broke and the builders on the hill fled. Xianbi drove straight for the siege lines while the defenders of Yiyang sallied out again.
At dawn Ma Xianpin came as Yong had foreseen. Zhang Huai's line broke and the builders on the hill fled. Xianpin drove straight for the siege lines while the defenders of Yiyang sallied out again.
馬仙琕: 琕 is read pín. Short form corrected as well.
Yong left part of his force with Chief Administrator Jia Sizu to hold the camp and led a thousand horse and foot south to meet Xianbi.
Yong left part of his force with Chief Administrator Jia Sizu to hold the camp and led a thousand horse and foot south to meet Xianpin.
馬仙琕: 琕 is read pín.
He cut across the enemy line. A bowshot pierced his left thigh; he pulled out the arrow and plunged back in, routed the enemy, and took the head of Xianbi's son.
He cut across the enemy line. A bowshot pierced his left thigh; he pulled out the arrow and plunged back in, routed the enemy, and took the head of Xianpin's son.
馬仙琕: 琕 is read pín.
Xianbi burned his camps and fled in haste.
Xianpin burned his camps and fled in haste.
馬仙琕: 琕 is read pín.
The case went to the Ministry of Education. Minister Hu Guozhen had campaigned with Yong and, moved by Yong's own wishes, allowed Shuwei's burial plan.
The case went to the Minister of Education. Minister Hu Guozhen had campaigned with Yong and, moved by Yong's own wishes, allowed Shuwei's burial plan.
事經司徒: 司徒 is the Minister of Education.
Before long he was relieved of the commandery, returned as Grandee of the Palace, acted in charge of Southern Qing Province, and was promoted to Left General and Inspector of Southern Yan Province.

Before long he was relieved of the commandery, returned as Grand Master of Palace Counsel, acted in charge of Southern Qing Province, and was promoted to Left General and Inspector of Southern Yan Province.
太中大夫 is Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
When he returned to the capital, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
When he returned to the capital, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master for Splendid Virtue.
光祿大夫 is Grand Master for Splendid Virtue.
He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qi Province.
He was posthumously granted General Who Calms the East and Inspector of Qi Province.
安東將軍 is General Who Calms the East (平東 is Pacifies).
You's son Zun served Shi Hu as Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
Zhou's son Gou served Shi Hu as Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
伷 is Zhou; 遘 is Gou.
When Liu Jun's generals Xiao Bin and Wang Xuemo attacked Que'ao, Rong had just died. Xuemo pressed Lingqing into service as army leader.
When Liu Jun's generals Xiao Bin and Wang Xuanmo attacked Que'ao, Rong had just died. Xuanmo pressed Lingqing into service as army leader.
王玄謨 is Wang Xuanmo. Short form corrected as well.
Bin and Xuemo ordered men after him.
Bin and Xuanmo ordered men after him.

His cousin Qian'ai served Xiao Bin as legal aide. Bin sent Qian'ai to summon Lingqing with a waist-knife as token and secretly ordered strong men to follow. Qian'ai did not know Bin meant to kill him.

His father's cousin Qian'ai served Xiao Bin as legal aide. Bin sent Qian'ai to summon Lingqing with a waist-knife as token and secretly ordered strong men to follow. Qian'ai did not know Bin meant to kill him.
從叔 is a paternal uncle of the collateral line.
Lingyue was made General Who Pacifies the Distant, Governor of Qingzhou, and Baron of Beiqiu, with his seat at Yanglan Fort.
Lingyue was made General Who Guards the Distant, Governor of Qingzhou, and Viscount of Beiqiu, with his seat at Yanglan Fort.
鎮遠將軍 is Guards the Distant; 貝丘子 is a viscountcy.
Guangzhi sent him alive to Liu Yu's Pacification Headquarters aide Liu Yan.
Guangzhi sent him alive to Liu Mian, adjutant in Liu Yu's headquarters of the General Who Supports the State.
劉勔 is Liu Mian; 輔國府司馬 is an adjutant of the Supports-the-State HQ.
Yan received him with courtesy and asked why he had rebelled. He answered, "The Nine Provinces rose in righteous cause. How could that be mine alone?"
Mian received him with courtesy and asked why he had rebelled. He answered, "The Nine Provinces rose in righteous cause. How could that be mine alone?"
Yan asked again, "Rebels everywhere are taken in every battle, and the throne has shown great mercy, using each man's gifts. Why did you not return to court instead of hiding in the wild?"
Mian asked again, "Rebels everywhere are taken in every battle, and the throne has shown great mercy, using each man's gifts. Why did you not return to court instead of hiding in the wild?"
Yan admired his bearing and sent him on to Jiankang.
Mian admired his bearing and sent him on to Jiankang.
After he entered Wei, Prince Su of the Southern Garrison was struck by him and admired his father's integrity. Su treated him with full courtesy and had him appointed as an aide.
After he entered Wei, Wang Su, General Who Guards the South, was struck by him and admired his father's integrity. Su treated him with full courtesy and had him appointed as an aide.
鎮南王肅 is Wang Su the 鎮南將軍, not a prince.
He followed Su on campaign and won repeated distinction, rising to palace attendant, colonel of foot soldiers, and Left General of the Household, and often commanded armies in the east and west.

He followed Su on campaign and won repeated distinction, rising to palace attendant, colonel of foot soldiers, and Leader of Court Gentlemen of the Left, and often commanded armies in the east and west.
左中郎將 is Leader of Court Gentlemen of the Left.
Later the Di chieftain Yang Jiyi of Wuxing rebelled, enthroned his nephew Shao, and besieged Guancheng.
Later the Di chieftain Yang Jiyi of Wuxing rebelled, enthroned his nephew Shaoxian, and besieged Guancheng.
兄子紹先 is his nephew Shaoxian.
Taihong led thousands of Di and Shu against Guancheng. Fu Shuyan sent General Who Pacifies the North Cheng Xingsun to meet him.
Taihong led thousands of Di and Shu against Guancheng. Fu Shuyan sent General Who Calms the North Cheng Xingsun to meet him.
寧朔將軍 is General Who Calms the North.
At Baihu, Taihong sent Ren Shuo north with a thousand men to hold the passes, stringing three camps along the southern slopes of Tiger Pass.
At Baihu, Taihong sent General Who Supports the State Ren Shuobei and others with a thousand men to hold the passes, stringing three camps along the southern slopes of Tiger Pass.
任碩北 is a personal name; 輔國將軍 omitted.
Cui Liang of the Pacification Headquarters attacked him and made Fu Shuyan holder of the staff and army secretary of the Southern Garrison.
Cui Liang, General Who Guards the South, attacked him and made Fu Shuyan holder of the staff and army supervisor to the General Who Guards the South.
鎮南將軍 is a title held by Cui Liang; 鎮南軍司 is his army supervisor.

On arrival he was made Right General and Governor of Yizhou, then Attendant Cavalier at Leisure, General Who Pacifies the West, and lent commander of the western campaign with three thousand troops against Zhang Qi.

On arrival he was made Right General and Governor of Yizhou, then Attendant Cavalier at Leisure, General Who Pacifies the West, acting General Who Calms the West, and Commander-in-Chief of the Western Campaign with three thousand troops against Zhang Qi.
假安西將軍、西征都督 omitted / mistranslated.
He sent Fu Yanbiao and others to crush Wang Guangzhao, Liang's General Who Pacifies the North, at Yinping.
He sent Fu Tanbiao and others to crush Wang Guangzhao, Liang's General Who Calms the North, at Yinping.
傅曇表 is Fu Tanbiao; 寧朔 is Calms the North.
Fu Shuyan asked to leave Yizhou but was refused. He was made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Qi, retaining his attendant title.
Fu Shuyan asked to leave Yizhou but was refused. He was made General Who Calms the West and Governor of Qizhou (岐州), retaining his attendant title.
安西 is Calms the West; 岐州 is Qizhou, not Qi (齊).
Soon he was lent General Who Pacifies the Army and supreme commander over Liang, western Yi, and Ba.
Soon he was lent General Who Guards the Army and supreme commander over Liang, western Yi, and Ba.
鎮軍將軍 is General Who Guards the Army.
In the Yong'an era he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East, Minister of Personnel, and Governor of Qi.
In the Yong'an era he was posthumously made General Who Subdues the East, Minister of Personnel, and Governor of Qi.
征東將軍 is General Who Subdues the East.
At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously raised to Attendant Cavalier at Leisure, General of the Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Governor of Xiangzhou, with his fief unchanged.

At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously raised to Attendant Cavalier at Leisure, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Governor of Xiangzhou, with his fief unchanged.
車騎將軍 is General of Chariots and Cavalry.
His eldest son Jinghe and younger son Jingzhong were both drunkards of poor character who curried favor with the powerful.
His eldest son Jinghe and Jinghe's younger brother Jingzhong were both drunkards of poor character who curried favor with the powerful.
敬和弟敬仲: Jingzhong is Jinghe's younger brother.
Jinghe served as chief administrator of the Qingzhou Pacification Headquarters.
Jinghe served as chief administrator of the Qingzhou headquarters of the General Who Guards the Distant.
鎮遠府長史 refers to the Guards-the-Distant HQ.
Fan Wench of Liang besieged him; Jinghe surrendered the city and was sent south of the Yangzi.
Fan Wenchi of Liang besieged him; Jinghe surrendered the city and was sent south of the Yangzi.
Qian'ai's son Sanbao, with Fang Fashou and others, won merit at Panyang Note marker [7] and was ennobled Baron of Beiqiu.
Qian'ai's son Sanbao, with Fang Fashou and others, won merit at Panyang Note marker [7] and was ennobled Viscount of Beiqiu.
Sanbao's younger brother Faxian defected south early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign and became Xiao Luan's Right General of the Household and inner-guard commander.
Sanbao's younger brother Faxian defected south early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign and became Xiao Luan's Leader of Court Gentlemen of the Right and inner-guard commander.
右中郎將 is Leader of Court Gentlemen of the Right.
He saw action early, and his cousin Chong thought highly of him.
He saw action early, and his elder paternal cousin Li Chong thought highly of him.
從兄崇 is the elder paternal cousin Li Chong.
He became General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Chenliu, commanding the Diqiu garrison.
He became General Who Tranquilizes the Distant and Administrator of Chenliu, commanding the Diqiu garrison.
寧遠將軍 is Tranquilizes the Distant (安遠 is Pacifies).
In the Xiaochang era he acted as governor of Xiangzhou, was soon confirmed, and was given General Who Comforts the Army, lent General Who Pacifies the East, and made Grand Commander-in-Chief.
In the Xiaochang era he acted as governor of Xiangzhou, was soon confirmed, and was given General Who Comforts the Army, lent General Who Guards the East, and made Grand Commander-in-Chief.
鎮東將軍 is General Who Guards the East.

Earlier the provincial commander Yuan Jian had rebelled and invited the rebels in. Later Commander Yuan Ziyin and Pei Yan were defeated and killed. The court and country were terrified and no one felt safe.

Earlier the provincial commander Yuan Jian had rebelled and invited the rebels in. Later Commander Yuan Ziyong and Pei Yan were defeated and killed. The court and country were terrified and no one felt safe.
He was made General of the Cavalry and, for his service, advanced to duke with eight hundred added households, bringing his fief to one thousand in all.
He was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and, for his service, advanced to duke with eight hundred added households, bringing his fief to one thousand in all.
車騎將軍 is General of Chariots and Cavalry.
In Putai year one he was advanced to General of the Valiant Cavalry with honors equal to the Three Excellencies and made chief rectifier of Xiangzhou.
In Putai year one he was advanced to Grand General of Agile Cavalry with honors equal to the Three Excellencies and made chief rectifier of Xiangzhou.
驃騎大將軍 is Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
In Tianping year one he was posthumously granted the staff of authority, made attendant within the palace, General of the Valiant Cavalry, Minister of Education, and Governor of Jizhou.
In Tianping year one he was posthumously granted the staff of authority, made attendant within the palace, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Education, and Governor of Jizhou.
驃騎大將軍 is Grand General of Agile Cavalry.

Editorial note: "He went to Chang'an to worship at the temple of the civilized empress's father, Prince Yan of Xu"—some editions add ling after "temple"; the Beishi biography of Fu Yong, juan 45, does not.

Editorial note: "He went to Chang'an to worship at the temple of Empress Dowager Wenming's father, Prince Xuan of Yan"—some editions add ling after "temple"; the Beishi biography of Fu Yong, juan 45, does not.
文明太后父燕宣王 is Feng Lang, Prince Xuan of Yan.
Grants of office and noble rank for worship at Prince Yan of Xu's temple appear often in the biographies of Zheng Yi (juan 56), Yang Zao (juan 72), Li Shu (juan 72), and Gao Zun (juan 89).
Grants of office and noble rank for worship at Prince Xuan of Yan's temple appear often in the biographies of Zheng Yi (juan 56), Yang Zao (juan 72), Li Shu (juan 72), and Gao Zun (juan 89).
燕宣王 is Prince Xuan of Yan.
